findings: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp: the only change is a reordering. JoinDependentFilterRule is now registered just before DistributivityRule instead of after it. Before, DistributivityRule factored the shared join-key term out of the root OR, so JoinDependentFilterRule's root-OR precondition never held for predicates like q19's. The change does not mention any query, table, column or literal.

Correctness: the rule (src/optimizer/rule/join_dependent_filter.cpp) keeps the original OR intact and ANDs implied single-table OR filters onto it. It skips volatile expressions and only derives a filter for a table that appears in every branch. Moving it earlier does not change what it is allowed to derive, so NULLs, other types and volatile functions behave as before.

Termination: the rule only fires when the root expression is an OR (`is_root`). Its output root is an AND, so it cannot fire again on its own result and there is no rewrite loop. DistributivityRule still runs afterwards on the inner OR.

Scope: this applies to any OR-of-conjunctions filter or ANY_JOIN condition that spans several tables, such as TPC-H q07/q19 and BI-generated SQL. It is not narrow to this benchmark. Nothing moves cost elsewhere, no measurement code is touched, and no code is duplicated.
Minor caveat: the author did not run the optimizer or plan-snapshot unit tests. Some EXPLAIN-based tests may show the extra derived filters, but that is a plan change, not a correctness problem.
